job: Complete Sentiment Desk as a real-data-only research desk for serious individual investors and professional analysts. Deliver useful no-ticker discovery, fundamental research-worthiness, and followed-company material-change workflows; use OpenAI GPT-6 Luna for new public-source classifications while preserving historical Jev judgments; keep public-company source, time, rights, spend, privacy, and recovery controls truthful; include optional user-owned private evidence only for configured publicly listed issuers, never private-company coverage; meet the frozen investor and AlphaSense outcomes; keep Opportunity Radar disabled until operational acceptance passes; and push reviewed checkpoints to the existing branch.
acceptance: Master Eval compares Sentiment Desk with AlphaSense on 30 prospectively registered real 7-day retail/consumer inflection tasks across at least 15 issuers and 6 sectors, under the same task, UTC cutoff, and 20-minute analyst interaction allowance. Preserve versions, access, outputs, sources, timestamps, cost, and latency. Two blinded subagents use separately initialized contexts and distinct configured models where available; do not claim independent model families without verified lineage. A third blinded subagent adjudicates disagreements without selecting a new outcome after seeing which product leads. A valid no-signal result states searched scope/window, actual coverage and freshness, material gaps, uncertainty, and next check; it is neither an automatic win nor an automatic error. Missing, malformed, and unsupported outputs cannot win and remain in task and error denominators. Report missing, invalid, no-signal, and supported-signal outcomes per product, with material errors per task and per asserted claim. A Desk win requires at least one additional material, source-verified decision-relevant signal absent from AlphaSense, supported by eligible point-in-time evidence from at least two independent origins, not duplicated or unresolvedly contradicted, and accompanied by a concrete next check. Comparator wins are symmetric; if each product has a unique supported material finding, the task is a tie. Freeze issuer, shared-event, and time dependence clusters, the paired inference method, and both decision thresholds before output review; prefer one event per issuer. A pass requires both the two-sided exact paired test and the predeclared dependence-aware paired inference to support a Desk advantage at p<0.05. If defensible dependence-aware inference is unavailable, leave the statistical result UNVERIFIED; a completed non-supportive cluster-aware result is FAIL. Report error rates both per task and per asserted claim, with denominators fixed before review. Pass only with 30 completed paired tasks, at least 10 Desk wins, at most 2 AlphaSense wins, >=80% pre-adjudication task-outcome agreement, both significance gates, and no higher material factual/entity/source/timestamp error rate. Agent agreement is reviewer-reliability evidence, not human ground truth; correlated model errors remain a limitation. This narrow test does not establish broad superiority, investment returns, retention, or release readiness. No access/output means BLOCKED; incomplete results are UNVERIFIED.

The product must help serious individual investors, including the owner, and professional analysts complete three real-data tasks: (1) discover companies worth investigating with no ticker, thesis, upload, or prepared dataset, including the stated small-cap and long-term fundamental focus; (2) decide whether a selected company merits more research by inspecting relevant drivers, supporting and contradictory evidence, uncertainty, missing information, and a concrete next question; and (3) identify a material change in a followed company against its prior baseline, with event/retrieval times, independent-source and duplicate disclosure, uncertainty, and a next check. A followed-company baseline is created only by an explicit user action and is persisted as an immutable, per-company version containing the exact saved observation IDs captured. The snapshot includes only identified real-source observations joined to a matching immutable delivery receipt whose result is success or partial and whose required ingestion has a terminal success or partial outcome. It excludes demo, synthetic, legacy_unknown, unreceipted, failed, and incomplete-ingestion records. Recapture appends a new version and preserves earlier baselines; capture requests are idempotent and reject a stale expected baseline. Comparison uses exact observation-ID membership and bounded keyset pages tied to company, baseline, and a fixed read snapshot; eligible and withheld totals stay stable across pages. It reports 'newly eligible saved source evidence', separately labels records whose ingestion finalized after the baseline despite earlier retrieval, and never presents that eligibility change as a material change or trading conclusion. It preserves the source URL, judgment status, publisher time, provider-observed time, retrieval time, and ingestion-completion time. A source published before the baseline but retrieved after it is labeled as a late arrival. A source retrieved before the baseline but accepted by terminal ingestion afterward is labeled as late-finalized, not newly collected. Pending evidence remains visibly pending. Baseline reads and writes make no provider or classifier calls. No-baseline, empty, loading, stale, and failed states remain distinct; retry, pagination, and reset are keyboard accessible and the rendered view has no horizontal overflow at 390px. Verify these paths in the actual UI with intended users without coaching; record completion, time to a source-checked result, corrections, and remaining effort. At least five serious individual investors and five professional analysts each attempt all three tasks; pass requires at least 80% uncoached completion per task and audience, median time to a source-checked result no greater than ten minutes, zero critical source, entity, or time errors, and no more than one user-reported factual correction per completed task. Product-owned sources must be acquired programmatically under verified source rights. The no-ticker start cannot rely on the fixed 24-company list, unexplained counts, stale history, or Radar expansion. Never label a company small-cap without an eligible point-in-time price and dated shares-outstanding basis, explicit corporate-action handling, and a source-linked market-cap band; preserve accession, accepted time, reporting period, units, and amendment lineage for SEC fundamental facts.

New observations and research reads use identified real sources; demo and synthetic records never enter product runtime, and legacy_unknown rows stay quarantined from research and Jev paths. The 4,700 historical legacy_unknown observations remain excluded until their source and any classifier/provider usage are reconciled against original provider request and account-usage/billing records; do not infer provenance or billing from row shape or timestamps. SEC extraction prioritizes actual numbered 8-K sections over the cover page, is deterministic and bounded, and versions newly persisted receipts without modifying historical records. For new Item 2.02 filings, the source adapter selects only a unique same-accession HTML Exhibit 99.1 explicitly identified by the visible results section, preserves bounded primary/exhibit request evidence outside classifier input, and emits no observation for incomplete acquisition. Legacy receipts, stable input revision semantics, prompt/schema/profile and historical judgments remain unchanged.

OpenAI GPT-6 Luna is the selected classifier for new records, using strict categorical outputs with exact prompt/schema/request/response provenance and complete usage. No Luna category is converted into a Jev probability, confidence or impact value, or mixed into legacy numeric charts, reaction memory or threshold alerts. Missing credentials, source/account approval or finite budgets leave items pending without TypeSafe fallback. Unknown outcomes retain their reservation and require operator review. A public FinEntity sentiment-only diagnostic is run using only rights-cleared real benchmark data whose use permits OpenAI transmission, local scoring, and retention. Its versioned rights, eligible paragraph-target rows, exact request digests, frozen GPT-6 Luna prompt/schema/profile, returned model, response digests, per-row usage, and run timestamps are digest-bound; report per-class precision, recall and F1, confusion, coverage, selective accuracy, abstention-inclusive accuracy, missing/failed/invalid/abstained denominators, cost, latency, and paragraph-cluster uncertainty. The benchmark evaluator is offline and never returns a classifier-quality PASS: a valid sentiment-only result remains UNVERIFIED and cannot establish source grounding, citation entailment, entity/period/unit/numeric correctness, justified abstention, completeness, or investment utility; protected workflow cases own those claims. Missing or invalid benchmark rights, rows, profile, or persisted Luna output is BLOCKED. A frozen real SEC cohort of at least30 cases across at least8 configured issuers binds two independent blinded agent reference sets to the exact new prompt and request profile. Predeclared diagnostic targets remain macro-F1>=0.80, represented-class precision/recall>=0.70 and inclusion precision>=0.90 with all3 sentiment classes represented; unresolved and failed cases remain in the denominator. Agent agreement is separate from human ground truth and statistical certification. A missing API credential, live run, usage reconciliation or source/reference evidence blocks live qualification; no quality pass is inferred from fixtures.

A successful OpenAI response is accepted as Luna only when the returned model and actual service tier exactly match the prepared GPT-6 Luna profile. A mismatch is withheld from categorical persistence and charts, leaves the observation failed for usage review, and preserves response ID, digest, returned model/tier, tokens, and cost evidence when available. The Desk persistence method verifies the complete response receipt; a SQLite insert trigger binds the classification to its explicit saved attempt ID and exact model, requested/actual tier, prompt/profile/schema digest, HTTP response, response ID/digest, token counts, cost, and latency. The guard installs idempotently during the additive version-9-to-version-11 migration without rewriting historical rows; legacy classifications with no attempt-bound profile remain visible in history but excluded from categorical trends.

The selected-company chart defaults to Luna categories and remains there while its matching company/window snapshot is loading, failed, or contains eligible source-linked Luna classifications. After a successful matching zero-count snapshot only, perform one bounded local saved-archive lookup. Keep Luna selected while that lookup is pending, failed, mismatched, or returns no eligible scores. Once a populated archive for the same company is confirmed, keep Luna selected and show a deliberate, dated Historical Jev action with the exact archive week, saved-score count, and latest-score time; the archive is available only after explicit action or tab selection, and is never treated as current Luna sentiment. If the archive is empty or unavailable, retain the truthful Luna empty/error state and its saved-source recovery action. If Older/Newer archive navigation is loading or fails, keep the last verified same-company archive week and chart visible, mark that week as stale/refresh-failed, and never let the request status hide a valid result; discard it only after a confirmed empty result or company change. Retry one automatic archive read after a transient failure, then stop until an explicit retry or a new backend runtime. The Luna chart remains the primary automatic view before and after new classifications arrive. A receipt-linked Luna classification event while an explicitly selected same-company Jev archive is visible may trigger one bounded, debounced local Luna-snapshot refresh so returning to Luna shows current saved classifications; recurring polling remains limited to the active chart. Manual tab choices continue to override automatic selection. When no eligible source-linked Luna classifications are saved, show a truthful empty state rather than neutral sentiment, with the primary action opening the selected company’s saved source feed and a separate explicit action for historical Jev. The selected company’s saved evidence summary appears immediately after the active chart and before optional SEC fundamentals or baseline panels; its record action preserves company and window, opens and focuses the real saved source feed, and honors reduced-motion settings. Any explicit chart-tab choice persists across polling, selected evidence-window changes, and delayed archive replies for the same company; changing the selected company resets the view to automatic Luna. Historical Jev is visibly labeled as archived model output, not current Luna or independently validated investor opinion. When Historical Jev is visible, the selected-company summary reports the same UTC archive week and scored-record count as the plotted chart, explicitly identifies the archive UTC interval, and labels the selected rolling Luna/source evidence window separately. The visible controls are labeled as the current saved evidence window; in Historical Jev view they do not imply a shorter plotted archive range. The historical-action summary never borrows counts from the rolling Jev series. Luna counts include only complete, receipt-linked, real GPT-6 Luna source observations by classification-availability time. Positive, neutral, negative, review-required, and excluded are the five reachable outcomes; absent direction maps to review-required. The client may group canonical 15-minute values into UTC-aligned 30-minute, 1-hour, 3-hour, or 6-hour display intervals, but each displayed category and total reconciles exactly to the canonical snapshot and its paginated source records through the matching half-open evidence span. Seven days show at most 29 intervals; earlier values stay inside the chart's keyboard-scrollable region, with no page overflow at 320px or 390px. Date labels show UTC, seconds, milliseconds, and exclusive end semantics. Lightweight Charts receives strictly increasing fractional Unix-second timestamps derived directly from safe integer UTC milliseconds; duplicate or malformed endpoints are rejected rather than shifted. Prompt/schema lineage and mixed-profile caveats remain visible. Empty, refreshing, failed, and stale-snapshot states remain distinct; a refresh failure after an empty read is unknown, not current-empty. Restarted snapshots recover automatically and do not strand selected evidence. Tab changes preserve the selected interval and poll only the active chart, except for the single event-triggered local snapshot refresh that keeps hidden Luna data current when the user has explicitly selected Historical Jev. Luna never reuses Jev impact, decay, price, probability, or confidence semantics. Its saved categorical snapshot reads are local and do not call an AI classifier provider; the separate Yahoo market-price panel may refresh only through the existing bounded, per-source-approved market-data acquisition path. In the selected-company Luna view, show a separately titled real Yahoo market-price context panel regardless of whether Luna is loading, failed, empty, or populated. On wide screens it sits beside the Luna chart or empty state. On narrow screens, keep Luna first when saved categories exist; if the matching zero-count snapshot is loading or failed, or a confirmed empty snapshot has no categories, place a receipt-verified price chart first when available and keep the empty/error Luna state and source-review action explicit. Without verified points, do not invent a price chart. It never shares a sentiment scale or substitutes for sentiment, and it uses only receipt-verified observations with no values carried across gaps longer than six hours.

The historical Jev impact view uses only saved real scored observations. Each nonempty UTC 15-minute bucket displays the deterministic weighted mean of the actual Jev impacts, scored-record count, and observed minimum and maximum; missing buckets remain gaps, and neither the company chart nor watchlist sparkline connects, carries forward, decays, or extends values between observations. The chart visibly states that buckets are keyed to Jev score-completion time, not publication time, public discussion volume, investor activity, or price, that repeated coverage can count again, and that a prominent chart-level cue tells readers to inspect bucket lineage before interpreting a bar. Hover inspection and the keyboard-accessible data table show each populated bucket’s receipt-linked count against its exact record count and the rows in repeated normalized-title groups; title matches are explicitly described as cues, not proof of duplicate stories or independent origins. Selected-bucket details expose source clocks and delivery-receipt links before interpretation. The selected bucket also exposes a full 20-bin unweighted histogram whose counts sum to the full bucket count, with +100 in the final bin; source-list pagination is disclosed separately. Bucket counts reconcile to exact saved source-record drilldown. Historical freshness and profile remain distinct from Luna categories, and price is omitted unless provenance is verified. A routine rolling-window refresh cannot mark a selected fixed historical archive bucket as expired; archive evidence is rechecked against the matching archive week instead.

Historical impact-band filtering uses the exact full saved UTC bucket snapshot before source-row pagination: the 20 bands are half-open [−100+10i, −90+10i), with +100 included only in the final band. Filtering never changes the full interval count, weighted mean, observed spread, or 20-bin histogram; matchingRecordCount and filtered source rows are reported separately. Every page cursor is bound to company, interval, snapshot, and selected band. Changing bands discards stale responses; zero-match and clear-all states recover accurately, with clear-all restoring the full snapshot. Verify against real saved bucket data, including a selected band whose matching records extend beyond the unfiltered first page. Every accepted historical Jev bucket response also reports full-bucket exact-normalized title count, records in repeated exact-title groups, untitled records, score-completion range, publisher-declared and provider-observed source-time counts/ranges separately, unknown-basis counts, and delivery-receipt links. It is calculated from immutable source-observation fields inside the accepted bucket snapshot, remains unchanged across impact filtering and source-row pagination, preserves missing/unknown clocks as unknown, and the UI says score-completion buckets are not 15-minute measures of publication volume or investor activity. It is withheld with a reload action if malformed or inconsistent. An initial detail-load failure shows only the actual failure and retry, never a stale chart count or an unobserved distribution claim.

Feed failures, pending judgments, and retries remain persistent, bounded, recoverable, and reachable to the user, including aggregate alert attention counts, prioritized pageable outcomes, responsive source/operations health details, and a visible not-configured webhook state before the first alert.

The selected-company source feed includes an explicit paginated History filter across all retained dates and eligible identified-real-source statuses, including off-target and unscored rows. Ordinary sentiment/status filters remain inside the selected window; History requests omit the time cutoff, sort newest source/observation/retrieval time first, preserve stable cursors, show the full available source date and timezone plus retrieval age, explicitly label missing source time, and never request provider data. Demo and legacy_unknown rows remain excluded. Empty and load-more states describe the selected company's retained history accurately.

Within the selected-company feed, pending scoreless rows with the same normalized title group only when their company also matches. Groups state that counts cover loaded rows, keep every original source row expandable, and describe title identity as a duplicate cue rather than independent-source proof. Other judgment states remain separate. Adjacent feed guidance and evidence-breadth metrics identify the scored/pending population each count summarizes; zero Jev-scored groups must not imply there are no pending repeat groups.

When an identified real observation is newly persisted, the live Desk stream emits its exact saved mention once before optional classification starts, so a pending row reaches an already-open feed without polling or reload. Exact replay and rejected persistence emit no mention event. Company source-count snapshots are refreshed through a coalesced update per changed company after ingestion yields; shutdown cancels the timer, and reconnect recovery returns the persisted snapshot.

At1440x900, the selected company, selected date/window, and active chart are visible without scrolling when available. Luna is the default; the Historical Jev chart appears only after explicit selection. At least three actual supporting source headlines are visible without scrolling when available. Company selection updates heading, chart and evidence; J/K keeps selection visible. Chart bucket inspection reaches real supporting records and the original source. At390px, there is no horizontal overflow. When only receipt-verified Yahoo price points are available for the selected company, place that real chart before the empty or unavailable Luna state; keep its source clocks and not-sentiment distinction visible, with saved-source review one direct action away. Expanded SEC filing triage must remain fully readable through vertical scrolling, without clipping. Verify selection, chart, and source drilldown in the rendered Codex in-app browser using real saved source records; a build, source inspection, or component-only test cannot pass this rendered-path criterion. Pending, historical, loading, error and true-empty states remain distinct, with truthful units, freshness and unvalidated-model disclosure. The Luna empty state keeps saved-source review as the primary action and, when historical Jev data exists, provides a separate action that states the actual saved score count and latest score time for the selected company and window before opening a clearly labeled historical chart; loading, empty, and unavailable history are reported truthfully. The watchlist identifies 24-hour source counts as retrieval-time counts; an empty selected source-time window explains the distinct time basis and, when recent retrieval exists, offers a separate direct route to the all-history unscored feed while preserving the normal full-feed action. SEC drawer judgment status and source lineage precede a collapsed excerpt, with the full source text still keyboard accessible. Source readiness is labeled separately from classifier judgment, SEC filing dates are shown as date-only calendar values; acceptance and retrieval timestamps retain their exact clock and UTC context, and pending items link to the classifier readiness details. For every selected company in the Luna view, show the selected company's Yahoo price context chart in the wide desktop first viewport without another chart-navigation action, regardless of Luna readiness or result count. Company and saved-source-window changes never leave points from the prior selection visible. During company-inventory loading, show a loading state instead of a zero-company empty state; after a confirmed load failure, disclose that inventory is unavailable. A true empty state is shown only after a successful empty response. When a latest quote is unavailable, label that quote state specifically so it is not confused with missing historical chart data.
The live-data contract and code-bound evidence are current and passing for the scoped live source/persistence path.
Opportunity Radar remains disabled until Sentiment Desk operational acceptance passes.
The verified cohesive checkpoint is pushed to the existing codex/real-data-rebuild GitHub branch.

A fresh installation with zero locally eligible saved observations receives a first-run API response containing only that local count and the current source/classifier readiness; no hard-coded archived company, filing, Jev output, digest, or demonstration observation appears in the response or UI. The Desk shows a clear true-empty state, keeps charts hidden when history is empty, and states the applicable next operator action without implying collection or classification is live. Demo/test and legacy_unknown rows do not make the local count nonzero. Loading and errors remain distinct from confirmed empty. A locally eligible saved observation removes the empty state immediately; stale or unverified provider state remains disclosed by its owning view. The read-only first-run path makes no provider requests, never affects research counts or calculations with an external archive, and does not mutate SQLite. Existing historical Jev records remain governed by their persisted local source provenance and are separate from new Luna categories. When local history arrives before company/feed snapshots catch up, the Desk refreshes once and retries bounded reads after transient snapshot errors without requiring reload.

The selected-company price context panel, independently of Luna readiness or result count while the Luna view is active, plots only receipt-verified Yahoo chart observations for the selected company and window. It remains separate from the active Luna chart and uses no sentiment scale. Price lines break at gaps longer than six hours; the chart never carries values forward or invents observations. It identifies company, ticker, currency, actual observation interval, source observation time, retrieval time, and delivery state, and provides a keyboard-accessible observation table with collection receipt IDs. Loading, confirmed empty, one-observation, malformed, transport-error, stale, and refresh-failed-with-saved-points states stay distinct. Its /price response carries a ticker-scoped count of legacy_unknown rows as disclosure metadata only; the count covers all local history, contains no legacy price or timestamp values, and cannot affect charts, calculations, refresh, freshness, or error status. A confirmed empty verified window distinguishes legacy rows withheld for incomplete provenance from a true zero count; missing metadata stays unknown, and stale/error/loading states never present an old count as current. Existing provider-failure and mixed-currency 502 behavior remains exact.

The SQLite storage boundary declares byte limits for the main database, complete SQLite file family, minimum free space, and reserved completion headroom. It applies and verifies the page ceiling before migration, measures the main/WAL/SHM/journal family and filesystem allocation, and checks capacity before each collector/model/webhook/price request and write. At the reserve boundary new external work stops without a failed provider receipt, while saved evidence remains readable and already admitted work may finish inside the reserve. A blocked reader prevents WAL truncation and therefore new external work; retry succeeds after the reader releases. At the hard page ceiling, writes fail with a typed storage-capacity error and the compatible database reopens read-only. The health API and operations UI show state, reason, measured files, limits, free space, and recovery action. Validate only in disposable SQLite databases; do not write test rows into the user's product database. The resource bound assumes a single application writer; multi-process and host-wide quotas remain outside the claim.

The selected-company SEC CompanyFacts view supports real-data triage for a configured issuer. It saves only accession-linked facts with matching issuer identity, submission form, filing date and acceptance time; stores the SEC payload digest and retrieval clock; and labels the fact interval from its own start/end dates, keeping filing fiscal-focus metadata separate. Period identity is exact company, taxonomy, concept, unit, start/end, and duration. Differing values, unresolved rows whose accession cannot be matched, malformed period data, amendments and truncated vintages are surfaced as coverage gaps and withheld from comparisons. Comparisons require both facts in the same filing, known acceptance times, the same entity, form, taxonomy/concept/unit/duration, and a unique prior candidate after identical duplicates are resolved. Accept exact one-calendar-year alignment or exact matching 364/371-day shifts of both period boundaries only when both periods have the same duration; annual matches also require adjacent periods. Ambiguous, unequal-duration, amended, conflicting, cross-filing, asymmetric, or other shifted fiscal windows are withheld. The UI names 52/53-week boundary separation and shows both exact ranges and durations. The annual revenue chart preserves date spacing, breaks lines across missing or non-calendar-aligned periods, labels its linear value range and unit, and provides a keyboard-accessible table of source-returned values with their SEC precision status. The adapter retains `decimals` only if the CompanyFacts response supplies it; it never infers or applies precision as a scale. Missing precision leaves differences explicitly reported-value arithmetic and withholds percentage changes. Invalid precision withholds comparison. Percentage change is emitted only when both facts declare decimals=INF; finite-precision amounts remain reported-value differences without a point-percentage claim. For declared precision, a difference within the full sum of both reported increments has unresolved direction because SEC accuracy can reflect rounding or truncation. It withholds the plot when point units or metrics differ. Refresh is explicitly gated, bounded, idempotent and recoverable; partial zero-fact responses persist as partial, empty as empty, and failure preserves the last accepted snapshot. The UI shows only persisted real SEC values, filing links, the filing calendar date and distinct acceptance/retrieval timestamps, honest blocked/empty/stale/partial/failed states. Mark the saved view stale when its newest eligible matched filing acceptance is more than 365 days old or its latest SEC retrieval is more than 24 hours old, and state which clock triggered staleness; a fresh response retrieval never refreshes the filing observation. A filing triage states what a saved comparison supports, what it does not establish, and a concrete next check; when comparison is missing or ineligible, it explicitly reports that no supported material-change finding is available. Runtime product data and charts use only persisted real-source observations. Offline parser, comparison, persistence, and UI tests may use fictional, source-shaped facts only in bounded fixtures and temporary test databases; these never seed the product database, appear in the running app, or count as SEC source evidence. Local technical tests are not positive SEC-source proof: acceptance remains UNVERIFIED until an authorized real SEC response is saved and rendered in the actual Desk, including reload/failure-retention and mobile/keyboard checks. When the latest same-filing revenue facts include both comparable discrete-quarter and cumulative year-to-date periods with the same end date, the metric card labels and leads with the quarter, while preserving year-to-date as separate context; filing triage uses the most recent eligible quarterly comparison first and otherwise the most recent eligible revenue comparison. This slice does not establish no-ticker small-cap discovery, market-cap labels, materiality, investment merit or product completion. Place the selected-company chart and saved source evidence before the SEC fundamentals panel whether facts are populated or unavailable, so the primary chart and source-review path remain immediately scannable. When persisted real SEC facts exist, keep concise filing triage at the top of its panel; when facts are empty, unavailable, or blocked, state that truth and its next action in that same later panel. Keep the full metric grid, chart data, and coverage diagnostics in keyboard-accessible disclosure so a supported filing result is immediately scannable without letting an empty panel delay the primary investor workflow.

The selected-company source drawer supports a durable analyst-authored research queue over existing eligible identified real-source observations. From a source record, an analyst can save it for investigation with an optional next-verification question, or reversibly dismiss it from the working queue; neither action edits or deletes the immutable source. A dismissed source is hidden from the default selected-company working scan before keyset pagination. An explicit “Show set-aside” mode retrieves it with the disposition visible; live updates and reconnect reconciliation must not reintroduce it into the default scan. This analyst-only scan preference does not change saved-evidence samples, source history, tape, chart inputs, source counts, or immutable source data, which retain the real record. A disposition event carries no analyst note and causes no provider or classifier request. A first-class cross-company queue shows the exact source title, company, reported publisher, source link, existing judgment state, source and retrieval clocks, receipt-link status, and analyst-authored question, without model-authored synthesis, ranking, materiality, or recommendation claims. Queue state is keyed to the exact observation ID and company, persists across browser/server restart, and dismissal can be reversed from the source drawer. Invalid/non-real/demo/legacy_unknown observations, malformed or over-limit requests, and bounded-capacity overflow fail without partial writes. Reads and writes make no source or classifier requests. Loading, empty, failure, and populated states are distinct; the real UI is keyboard-operable and has no horizontal overflow at 390px. No synthetic or demo queue rows appear in the running product. This workflow is not evidence of issuer discovery, verified drivers, counterevidence, material change, or investment value.

Selected-company CompanyFacts acquisition is admitted only when the independent sec_company_facts request and source-use approval scopes both allow it, plus global external opt-in, a valid Sentiment Desk SEC User-Agent, storage admission, and the shared provider cooldown. This on-demand scope never starts scheduled 8-K polling; sec_edgar retains that separate roster-wide behavior, and neither scope implies the other. Process startup, company selection, saved-facts reads, and reload send zero SEC requests. Only an explicit same-origin JSON refresh for a configured company may acquire data, using at most three internally constructed official SEC GETs with the existing endpoint timeouts and byte limits; a process runs at most one selected-company refresh at a time. Cross-origin, non-loopback, cross-site, and non-JSON refresh requests fail before SEC work. New facts receipts use the sec_company_facts collector identity and are never eligible for Jev or Luna input. The UI explains that facts refresh is on demand and separates it from 8-K monitoring. A real selected-company workflow, persisted reload, previous-snapshot retention on failure, accessible evidence inspection, and actual source clocks remain required; scope enablement alone is not usability or source proof.

The zero-input interface offers a Recent Filings route for an investor who does not know a ticker. On a fresh local install with no eligible saved observations and no prior tab choice, the Desk opens this route. It reads only the Sentiment Desk profile from the authenticated local Public Data Hub and only a current-revision SEC `sec.latest_filings_8k` receipt served for `private_display`; export and redistribution remain disabled. The route is an unranked view of at most the newest 40 Form 8-K filings whose issuers are independently verified as currently exchange-listed by a current authoritative issuer directory; SEC reporting status, an issuer label, or a filing alone does not establish listed-company coverage. Unknown, stale, or unlisted issuers are withheld from the investor view with a count and exact listing-verification gap, and never create a company profile or research target. No private-company issuer is shown as covered. The route is with exact CIK/accession identity, a verified official SEC archive link, filing date and acceptance timestamp only when explicitly supplied, separate Atom update and Hub retrieval clocks, search, and distinct unavailable, unsupported, not-configured, pending, empty, stale, failed, and recovered states. Activating or refreshing is an explicit user action, requires both independent source allowlists and the global external-request gate, creates only the fixed 8-K profile with a cadence no faster than 15 minutes, and fails closed on identity, rights, URL, or receipt mismatch. No demo, synthetic, or other tenant feed is substituted.  Each filing also has one explicit in-app inspection action. It verifies the exact current inbox accession against the issuer CIK submissions record while preserving the submitting/accession CIK and archive-path CIK as separate values, then displays the official filing date, report period (never described as the event date), acceptance time, item codes, bounded readable primary text and only a uniquely linked same-accession Exhibit 99.1 when Item 2.02 requires it. Show SEC source URLs, retrieval clocks and content hashes; unresolved extraction remains visibly partial with retry and the official filing link. Inspection sends no text to a classifier, saves no body, and never runs for the whole inbox automatically. This source-browse path is a useful first step, but does not meet the separate full discovery requirement for small-cap candidates, fundamental triage, public adoption evidence, or an investment-opportunity ranking. When the filing feed is unsupported, unavailable, or failed without saved filing rows, the recovery action never opens an empty search: it offers Search saved archive only when eligible saved rows exist, clears stale company/history filters, and states that title/excerpt matches are historical leads rather than current coverage; when the archive is empty or unverified, it states that condition and offers a direct action to open Sources & operations.

For RSS-backed evidence from Google News RSS or Yahoo Finance RSS, a feed item's declared timestamp is recorded and displayed only as aggregator feed time; it never becomes verified publisher publication time, publisher-observed time, or article-age evidence. The UI labels article publication unknown and shows retrieval separately wherever those clocks affect interpretation. RSS records remain reviewable by retrieval chronology, but publication-based freshness, breaking events, alerts, publisher lag, and Radar eligibility/counts exclude them unless independent evidence supplies a publisher publication time. Existing immutable observations, observation IDs, receipts, historical classifier payloads/judgments, and followed baselines are preserved; known legacy RSS rows receive a deterministic read-time projection without rewriting source history. SEC acceptance-time semantics and scoring-time charts remain unchanged. Regression coverage uses only isolated fixtures and temporary databases; no demo/synthetic data enters runtime.

Historical Jev archive navigation opens the newest UTC week containing an eligible saved real Jev score, even when older than the current 7-day window. The latest-history choice and the plotted chart use the same eligibility rules: finite score time, finite impact in [-100,100], finite nonnegative weight, and score time inside the half-open week. The response is bound to exact company, week, UTC bounds and 15-minute buckets; the latest eligible score has an absolute UTC timestamp and age. Older/newer navigation skips empty weeks and a Latest action returns to the newest populated week. Bucket drilldown, impact bands, pagination, retry and stale-snapshot recovery remain bound to that exact chart snapshot. Global Luna, source-feed, market-price and other current windows do not change. Archive browsing reads saved local data only and makes no provider/model request. Price is withheld unless verified saved points match the exact archived week. No-history, loading, failure, empty or mismatched evidence remain distinct; keyboard and 320px/390px layouts work. Sparse populated weeks initially frame all eligible scored buckets inside the selected UTC week, with a visible exact half-open UTC plot-span label distinct from the selected archive week and touch-operable Fit scores and Full week controls of at least 44px; these controls expose all empty archive time without compressing score variation and never change records or the selected week. Verify the rendered journey using a protected copy of real local data, with isolated tests for eligibility, UTC/half-open boundaries, company/week races, and bucket reconciliation. Runtime contains no demo or synthetic observations.

Saved Sources gives an investor without a ticker two clearly separated read-only views. The recent tape shows at most the latest 60 real identified source observations returned by local /api/tape and is labeled incomplete for company history. Independently of that tape, a company picker lists every company in the configured 24-company desk inventory and lazily reads that company's retained identified real-source history from the paginated /api/companies/:id/mentions-page?filter=history endpoint, including records outside the latest 60 rows. The endpoint excludes demo and legacy_unknown records. Keyset pagination keeps older records reachable; search applies to every row already loaded; the separate Search archive view queries the complete retained source archive independently of loaded company-history pages. Company-history loading, confirmed empty, first-page failure, older-page failure, retry, and retained rows remain distinct. Session state preserves company selection, search, expanded result position, and per-company history-page depth. Returning to a company restores only pages already opened in the current tab and does not prefetch untouched history. Selecting or retrying a company performs local read-only requests and never starts provider collection or classification, writes a baseline, or mutates research data. Each row shows its desk ticker and publisher, a short saved source excerpt for triage, source-time basis and timestamp, a separate retrieval timestamp rendered visibly beside the source clock as an absolute time plus relative age, and a distinct Luna, historical Jev, pending, failed, or excluded state without implying independent validation. Represented companies are named in direct company filters with loaded-row counts, and local search also matches company names so an investor need not know a ticker or page through another issuer’s rows. A weak or missing issuerIdentityStrong result is visibly marked for issuer review instead of presenting that ticker match as established fact. A different exchange-prefixed, dollar-prefixed, or contextually explicit stock ticker in the headline or snippet creates a visible review cue even when the current name-based identity flag is strong; ordinary uppercase terms such as FDA or BTK do not count as tickers without stock context. A headline led by a different possessive company name creates the same cautious cue when its saved excerpt names the desk company. If that excerpt and the linked URL path also name the desk company, the interface specifically says to check title/link alignment while clarifying that a URL path does not verify page contents. These cues prompt relevance review and never assert that a multi-company source is unrelated or suppress the source. Reviewing a row opens that exact saved record in its issuer Desk. Visiting or retrying this route performs read-only requests only and never starts provider collection, writes a baseline, or mutates records. Loading, confirmed empty, failed, and stale-with-retained-data states remain distinct with a retry where useful. The interface says the view is bounded to this desk, not market-wide discovery or an opportunity ranking. When the SEC no-ticker feed is unsupported or unavailable, its recovery action opens Saved Sources. Verify with retained real local data in the rendered in-app browser at 1440, 390, and 320 CSS pixels, with zero horizontal overflow and no source-time/retrieval-time ambiguity; component tests alone do not pass the rendered journey. When an investor opens a saved row in its issuer Desk and closes its detail, returning to Saved Sources preserves the current search, company filter, and loaded-result position for the current tab, including when the source review switched issuers. Verify the full open-return journey with real retained records; a component remount test is supplemental. An already-open company-history cache incorporates matching real streamed observations immediately and is invalidated and reloaded after a runtime reset; late responses from a previous runtime cannot overwrite the refreshed view. Closing the record detail restores scroll position and keyboard focus to the exact reviewed row, with the Saved Sources heading as a safe fallback if that row is no longer available. A default Company coverage scan adds a balanced third read-only view at `/api/saved-source-coverage`: one stable SQLite snapshot includes every configured company and at most the newest three identified-real, non-dismissed rows passing the limited ambiguous-name identity gate per company; the stored company assignment and this gate do not prove that the article is about the issuer, along with exact retained-row and latest-retrieval counts. Rows failing the limited identity gate are excluded from the scan and counted separately for issuer review in full company history. The scan never labels assignment as verified article relevance. Company groups follow ticker order, never source volume or model score. The scan preserves the exact source and retrieval clocks, keeps row review linked to the existing source drawer and analyst question workflow, and offers direct navigation to full history. It makes no provider, classifier, or baseline request and writes no research data. Loading, empty, failed, and populated states are distinct. The archive coverage view labels its lookup time as a coverage snapshot and shows latest retrieval separately. Search results label their query cutoff as a search snapshot. Each repeated-headline group shows its newest retrieval, and expanded rows show each individual retrieval timestamp. The UI never implies that retained history is current, complete market coverage, or an opportunity ranking. Search archive finds title and excerpt matches across eligible real saved observations in the bounded 24-company archive without requiring a ticker, company selection, or loading company-history pages. Optional company, publisher, and dismissed filters apply to every page and count. A fixed snapshot cutoff excludes later-ingested records; a stable keyset cursor binds query, filters, source-time order, archive cutoff, and analyst-review revision. A changed review disposition invalidates further paging with an actionable restart message instead of silently changing counts or skipping records. Results order known source clocks exactly as displayed (publisher-declared, the applicable RSS feed-declared time, provider-observed); records with no source clock appear last, with retrieval time shown separately. Each result retains the stored company-assignment caveat, source/retrieval times, judgment state, source link, and exact-record review action. Search context and page position persist across source review; after results reload, the exact reviewed row receives restored scroll and keyboard focus, with a visible heading as fallback. Loading, no match, read failure, changed snapshot, retry, and restart are distinct and usable. The search is local read-only, starts no source, model, or baseline request, writes no research data, and excludes demo, synthetic, and legacy_unknown records. Two-character alphanumeric terms match whole words (so AI does not match inside Taiwan or daily); longer terms retain case-insensitive text matching. The cursor carries the matching-policy version; older cursors are rejected and the browser restarts at page one while preserving the query and filters. Verify the real saved-archive workflow in the rendered in-app browser at 1440, 390, and 320 CSS pixels with zero horizontal overflow and keyboard operation; component checks alone do not pass the rendered journey. If session storage access is denied, the application still opens with safe defaults and in-memory navigation and source review remain usable. Archive search results identify whether each query matched the headline, saved excerpt, or both, using the same whole-word rules as the server. On each returned page, adjacent rows on the same page with the same normalized headline and company assignment are grouped in their source-time order under a repeated-headline disclosure; every saved record remains individually inspectable with its source, clock, judgment state, and review action. The disclosure states that title similarity does not establish separate reporting, the page scope does not imply global event uniqueness, and result totals remain saved-record counts. This presentation does not change stored observations or make provider, classifier, or baseline requests.

User-owned private research material is an optional input only for an issuer already present in the configured publicly listed-company inventory with a curated listingStatus=publicly_listed marker enforced by config parsing and a runtime private-evidence issuer allowlist. Privately held companies are out of scope: no profile, discovery, monitoring, company count, ranking, or research target may be created for them. The local workflow accepts a manual note or UTF-8 .txt/.md/.csv up to 128 KiB per item and 40,000 Unicode code points, with a store-wide maximum of 250 items and 8 MiB; it stores exact text and SHA-256, explicit title/source, optional user-asserted date, import time, and optional basename in a dedicated owner-only SQLite directory. It does not infer source/event time from import time or file metadata. The store is not application-encrypted; OS snapshots or user backups may retain deleted copies. Only loopback-bound servers expose it, and server-side same-origin JSON checks and the configured public-issuer allowlist guard reads and writes. Private records never affect public sentiment, public source observations, counts, charts, baselines, alerts, public classifier input, logs, or automatic provider requests. Add/read/delete are local-only; private text is never sent automatically. A user may explicitly choose one saved item and use explicit in-app confirmation of its exact title, configured issuer, OpenAI GPT-6 Luna destination, response storage/caching behavior, and retention terms before processing. The Responses API request sets store=false, requests no prompt-cache breakpoints, uses no tools, and sends only that selected item and issuer identity. The locally stored result is bound to the selected note digest, preserves exact quoted evidence, uncertainty, model/profile/response hashes and usage, and never enters public sentiment. The result is analyst-only, not a verified fact or investment conclusion. Duplicate or uncertain attempts are not retried automatically. Missing credentials, account approval, operator enablement, external-request gate, writable storage, or finite shared OpenAI request/byte/USD caps leave the item unprocessed. Current account retention controls are unverified; the UI states OpenAI default API abuse-monitoring retention up to 30 days. Private uploads are never required for first-run discovery. No real user document was provided, so utility and quality on user material remain UNVERIFIED; tests use isolated temporary records only and no synthetic live data.

The offline GPT-6 Luna evaluation run binds every completed attempt to its exact bounded provider response bytes and SHA-256. The evaluator recomputes the digest, verifies response identity/status, structured classification and usage against those bytes, and rejects a saved prediction changed independently of the response. Reports omit raw response bodies. Validation makes no provider request and does not claim model quality without an actual persisted run.

A real current SEC 8-K can be saved as a durable My Research task keyed by exact CIK plus accession, with its official filing URL, optional analyst question, feed receipt, and separate observation/retrieval clocks. Two accessions for one issuer coexist; saving an existing task preserves its original source lineage while allowing question edits, and it can be resumed after feed rollover. New tasks require a ready current receipt. Failed saves preserve the draft; deletion affects only the selected filing. The workflow makes no classifier or source request. In read-only startup against an older schema lacking the task table, existing Desk reads continue while SEC task endpoints return an explicit unavailable response and the UI gives a retry/recovery action; the task list never masquerades as empty. Verify the real rendered My Research flow and durable state across restart when the preview is accessible.

A saved SEC filing task resumes the same CIK plus accession inside Desk after it leaves the latest inbox. The user can explicitly request inspection using only the server-stored official filing URL and its exact archive CIK path; task loading and resume make no SEC-document or classifier request. Stale, unavailable, paused, not-found, and failed evidence remain distinct with a direct recovery or official-source action. Updating a task without editing its question preserves that question, and invalid client URLs or unsaved rolled-out accessions cannot authorize SEC reads.

My Research lists the latest immutable company-research decision for each configured public issuer with its disposition, rationale, due/upcoming/no-date next-check status, saved time, exact evidence cutoff, and manifest counts. Opening it selects the same issuer and reconstructs only persisted evidence at the saved cutoff. The returned manifest digest must match the saved decision before evidence is shown; if historical evidence is unavailable or its digest differs, the UI withholds the brief and clearly offers retry rather than substituting newer evidence. Loading, empty, failure/retry, and unavailable-storage states stay actionable, keyboard focus reaches the brief, and existing source-record and SEC-filing queues remain usable. Resume makes no collector or provider request.

The selected-company next-research question exposes both exact accession-linked SEC facts behind its comparison even when latest-per-metric cards would hide one. Each fact shows reported value and unit, instant or full duration interval, filing form/accession, accepted and retrieved clocks, and SEC filing link; the caveat says reported-value arithmetic does not establish cause, business significance, or materiality.

The selected-company view offers keyboard-accessible direct actions to focus the source-bound research brief and open/focus that issuer's private-note panel. The concise decision action appears before both the detailed financial facts and public-source manifests; both long sections start collapsed. Private notes appear directly after the brief and before detailed fundamentals; every public-source lead row remains inspectable. Exact SEC fact-pair amounts retain full source precision with grouped digits, and essential labels, values, periods, and decision controls remain readable. At 1280×720, 390px, and 320px widths, the actions land on their intended sections with no horizontal overflow. A failed private-note read never claims that no content was saved; deletion confirms the exact note and issuer and cancellation sends no delete request.
owner: Jurgis owns the product decision and local deployment; source/account operators own their access attestations.

design.existing_patterns: Retain the existing TypeScript server, SQLite receipts and observations, bounded provider adapters, React/Vite research desk, offline startup verifier, and project-record ETL gate. The new SEC document evidence is an optional bounded receipt context, with no separate relationship service or new dependencies. For the Recent Filings workflow, preserve the compact list and expand exactly one selected filing inline so the investor can read its disclosure without losing issuer/accession context or navigating away. The selected row gets one bounded metadata request and at most the primary plus uniquely linked 99.1 document; store no body and dispatch no classifier. Keep filed date, report period, EDGAR acceptance and retrieval clocks as separately labeled fields; period is not event date. Show exact-source excerpt, URL, digest and partial/unavailable status.
design.data_ownership: Public provider source data remains under provider-specific access and retention rights; the user attested to rights for public sources and APIs, which is recorded as an operator attestation and does not itself prove an endpoint-specific provider contract, credential, billing record, or successful access. Local SQLite is operator controlled. Unknown-provenance historical rows remain quarantined. The first-run product surface reads only local saved evidence and readiness; it contains no hard-coded archived observation or demonstration result. Historical Jev records already persisted in SQLite remain separate from new Luna categories. New Luna classifications are product-derived data acquired through the user-selected OpenAI API route; the current verification environment has no direct OpenAI API credential and no finite provider spend readback, so live qualification is blocked. SEC parent and selected exhibit are product-managed public-source data; partial acquisition is operation evidence only and creates no pending model input. No-ticker discovery requires a product-owned issuer universe, SEC filing-backed fundamentals with point-in-time lineage, a maintained authorized price/shares/corporate-action basis for any market-cap label, and authorized public retail/consumer observations. A personal watchlist or thesis is user-owned and optional, never a prerequisite for first value. User-private evidence is stored separately under a restrictive owner-only local directory, bound to exact configured public issuer IDs, and excluded from all public observation, classifier, chart, alert, and provider paths. Its content is not encrypted by the application; this and deletion/backups limits are disclosed.
design.boundaries: Network collection and Jev forwarding default off; source and account approvals are distinct; the first-run endpoint reports the locally counted eligible observations and current collection/classifier readiness only; it never substitutes an out-of-installation archive or demonstration record. Live smoke uses a temporary isolated database; Radar stays disabled. The selected-company workspace reuses the existing request owners and recovery controller. Independent agent references use a separate v3 diagnostic mode; they never attest to human qualification or constitute ground truth. New OpenAI dispatch requires its own credential, account/source allowlists and daily request/byte/USD caps, default zero; TypeSafe is never an implicit fallback. New categorical rows have a separate persistence profile and terminal classified/excluded/review_required states. Historical probability records and quarantine remain unchanged. The zero-ticker discovery path is part of Sentiment Desk first value; it does not activate the separate Opportunity Radar. Do not rank companies using source counts alone or label stale history as a current opportunity. Selected-company facts use the separately requested and source-approved sec_company_facts scope; sec_edgar alone continues to control scheduled 8-K collection and neither scope implies the other. The facts scope never schedules work or forwards payloads to a classifier. A contact-only SEC_USER_AGENT is completed with the versioned Sentiment Desk identifier in process memory; the contact is never logged, persisted, or exposed to the UI. SEC disclosure inspection is a direct, explicit user action and is admitted only when the current inbox receipt contains the exact 8-K accession and the existing sec_edgar, sec_latest_filings_8k, global external-request, storage and SEC User-Agent gates are open. It makes one submissions request and at most two document requests, does not persist content or call Luna, and leaves the official index link available when paused, rate-limited or unresolved. The private-evidence API is disabled unless the server binds to loopback, requires same-origin JSON on mutations, and accepts only bounded UTF-8 text for configured public issuers. Add/read/delete make no provider request. Only an explicit selected-item confirmation can dispatch a private GPT-6 Luna analysis; that feature has its own default-off operator gate, uses the existing shared OpenAI daily request/byte/USD counters, begins a digest-bound one-attempt record before network dispatch, records ambiguous outcomes without automatic retry, and persists derived analysis only in the private store. Private text and derived analysis never enter public source tables, classifiers, charts, alerts, or company rankings.
design.simplicity: Use the existing React controls, formatters, tests, and verifiers; no new runtime dependency or synthetic product fixture is introduced. The private-evidence slice uses one small SQLite store and existing React/API patterns; it adds no parser or model dependency.

first_run.first_result_or_reason: With no ticker, thesis, upload, or user-built dataset, show a short current list of real listed companies worth investigating from the authorized product-owned universe. Each candidate must include filing-backed fundamental drivers and risks with an SEC accession identifier and filing date. Record the SEC acceptance timestamp, reporting period, unit, and amendment lineage as separate fields; include source-checked public adoption or dissatisfaction evidence; event and retrieval times; uncertainty; duplicate/independence status; and a concrete next research step. Label a company small-cap only when a point-in-time price, dated shares-outstanding basis, and corporate-action treatment support the displayed market-cap band. If that market-data basis is unavailable or stale, suppress the small-cap label and state the exact data gap. No static archived filing or classifier output substitutes for locally saved evidence. This zero-ticker value is not currently delivered: the saved preview has a fixed 24-company catalog, external requests disabled, no eligible Luna categories, and stale saved history. Never use synthetic data, source counts alone, or an empty chart to imply discovery value; the product remains blocked until qualifying real data is available. Until the complete issuer-universe discovery experience is qualified, a separate Recent Filings page supplies a bounded, real SEC filing-browse entry point without claiming small-cap status or investment merit; this does not close the broader discovery acceptance. Saved Sources offers a local archive scan with a balanced company-coverage view (up to three saved rows per tracked company passing a limited ambiguous-name identity gate; the gate is not content relevance verification), the separate latest-60 chronological tape, and lazily paged retained history for any configured desk company. The scan reports represented-company and retained-record counts, separates weak matches needing issuer review, and shows retrieval time; its ticker-ordered groups are not ranked. This stale-or-current saved archive is not issuer-universe discovery or opportunity ranking. The Search archive view searches titles and excerpts across the retained eligible records without requiring a ticker or previously loaded company pages, and is explicitly a back-catalog lookup rather than live opportunity discovery.
first_run.empty_or_blocked_state: Loading and API failure stay unknown, not empty. The first-run API reports the local eligible-observation count and selected source/classifier readiness only; it serves no out-of-installation archive or demonstration result. The current Luna chart shows an actual empty state only when the local count is zero and never plots archived model output or a fake gauge/chart. A separate Historical Jev tab may show only verified saved scores after the chart-selection rule above is satisfied. A newly arrived local observation suppresses the empty state immediately. Demo/test and legacy_unknown rows never qualify as research observations. Missing OpenAI credentials, account-use approval, or finite limits leave classification pending and do not trigger another provider. If exchange identity, SEC filing facts, current authorized price, dated shares-outstanding/corporate-action basis, or source-qualified public adoption evidence is unavailable, do not claim small-cap status, current fundamental coverage, or an absence of opportunities; show which dependency is missing, the covered company/source/time universe, as-of time, acquisition status, and next operator action. Never require a ticker or uploaded dataset merely to reach product-owned discovery. For a configured selected company, missing sec_company_facts approval keeps the explicit facts refresh blocked with the exact scope requirement; scheduled sec_edgar polling is a separate optional operation and must never be suggested as required for a one-company facts read. The SEC filing-browse entry distinguishes an absent Hub, unsupported dataset, missing profile, queued acquisition, true empty receipt, stale last-good receipt, refresh failure, and recovery. Source activation requires the global external-request switch plus the exact SEC 8-K entry in both independent allowlists; the route shows no substitute/demo rows, and retry is rate-limited. Saved-source coverage reads one bounded local snapshot across the configured companies, excludes demo, synthetic, legacy_unknown, dismissed, and rows failing the limited ambiguous-name identity gate from its sample, and reports weak-match counts separately. It shows the archive as-of and newest retrieval time, does not trigger collection or classification, and displays no sample rows when none qualify. The chronological tape remains capped at 60 and the selected-company endpoint continues to page the complete eligible history. Neither path starts collection or classification, writes a baseline, or mutates research data. Recent-tape empty, company-history empty, inventory loading or failure, history loading or failure, older-page failure, and stale retained rows remain distinct; retries are read-only.

change_safety.checkpoint: Root alone integrates reviewed worktree changes into codex/real-data-rebuild, pushes explicit in-scope source to the existing origin, and verifies the exact remote branch SHA. Restricted/raw runtime evidence stays local and ignored.
change_safety.rollback: Revert the new regular commit if required; preserve the local SQLite database and never roll back persisted user data to reverse source code. External requests remain off by default.

alignment.request: Complete the existing full real-data-only Sentiment Desk acceptance for serious individual investors and professional analysts: no-ticker discovery, fundamental research-worthiness, followed-company material change, source-grounded uncertainty and recovery; OpenAI GPT-6 Luna for new public-source classifications while preserving historical Jev semantics; real-source evaluation and AlphaSense comparison; truthful rights, provenance, time, account/spend, storage and empty states; responsive usable UI; no demo or synthetic live data; no Opportunity Radar expansion before operational acceptance; and regular reviewed GitHub checkpoints. Current correction: user-owned private evidence is in scope only as optional local research input to configured publicly listed issuers; private companies are out of scope for profiles, discovery, monitoring, counts and ranking. Keep that material separate from public sentiment; send a note to GPT-6 Luna only after an explicit confirmation naming the selected item and issuer. Preserve existing public-source, SEC/Compose, account, cost, freshness and release gates. All reviewer-based and real participant outcomes remain governed by the frozen acceptance thresholds; do not treat subagent agreement as human ground truth.
